Task: PREFERRED_LODGING_PARTNERSHIP_VENUE_DISCOVERY | Find businesses and venues near the hotel (verified hotel address, the hotel market) that could refer hotel guestrooms or groups — weddings, private celebrations, banquets, cultural/private functions, clubs, museums, entertainment destinations, and complementary event facilities. | A competing event venue can be a valuable Preferred Lodging partner when it has no guestrooms or only complementary / overflow lodging need. | Do NOT reject a venue merely because it offers meeting space, banquet halls, or catering — those often create overnight guest referral demand for a nearby hotel. | Prefer venues without a full competing guestroom inventory; still assess limited on-site lodging for overflow partnership potential (use UNKNOWN when not evidenced). | Exclude generic restaurants unless a documented event format credibly creates overnight visitors. | Return venue name, address, website, event types, on-site lodging status if published, and any lodging-partner language. | Do not invent distances, drive times, annual wedding counts, or room-night forecasts. | Venue types: wedding_reception_venue, standalone_banquet_hall, private_event_facility, independent_conference_event_venue, museum_event_rental, garden_or_historic_property, country_club_or_private_club_outside_events, cultural_institution_event_space, entertainment_destination_event_venue, waterfront_or_rooftop_event_venue

Task: PROFESSIONAL_EVENT_PLANNER_PARTNERSHIP_DISCOVERY | Discover actual planning companies, DMCs, meeting planners, and event-management businesses serving the hotel (verified hotel address, the hotel market) that can influence hotel bookings — guestroom blocks, wedding accommodation, banquets/catering, meeting space, private dining, or resort celebrations. | The commercial target is the planner / intermediary firm — not the conference, association, or host organization alone. | Conferences, galas, and published events are evidence of planner activity; use them to identify the credited planner, PCO, DMC, or event-management company. Do not substitute the conference brand for the planner identity. | Prioritize firms with evidence of recurring or multi-client event production and genuine hotel-sourcing influence — not directory popularity rankings. | Include planners physically based in the market AND planners demonstrably producing events in the destination even if their office is elsewhere. | Do NOT classify generic decorators, florists, photographers, equipment suppliers, or entertainment vendors as demand producers unless hotel-sourcing influence is independently evidenced. | Separate office location, verified service area, and actual event destination history. | Do not invent client counts, annual weddings, contracts, or production volume. | Local terminology: wedding planner; destination wedding planner; corporate event management company; event planning agency; meeting planner; boutique event producer | Channels: official_planner_websites, verified_planner_portfolios,
